      About this tradition

      What is BaZi?

      BaZi (八字, eight characters), also called the Four Pillars, is a Chinese tradition that records the year, month, day and hour of birth in the old sixty-pair calendar. Each pillar is one Heavenly Stem above one Earthly Branch, and each character belongs to one of the five elements: Wood, Fire, Earth, Metal and Water.

      The classical texts read a chart from the Day Master, the upper character of the day pillar. The pictures of the ten Day Masters on this page follow 滴天髓 (Di Tian Sui), and the names for how other characters relate to the Day Master, the Ten Gods, follow 淵海子平 (Yuan Hai Zi Ping). Each statement shows its source.

      Schools differ on a few settings, and Fate Tutor shows them openly: whether the day and hour use the sun's own time at the birthplace or the clock, and whether the day changes at 23:00 or at midnight. Without a birth time the hour pillar is left open rather than guessed.

      These are traditional systems of belief. They are not science and they do not predict the future. Fate Tutor shows what each tradition says and where it says it, in the language of tendencies.
